findings.reason: A concrete slit-domain picture materially clarifies why approaching the same removed segment above and below gives branch limits 0 and 2π, whereas an ambient smooth function has a single boundary value. The complete endpoint-estimate proof does not remove this explanatory benefit.
findings.action: Added a schematic and precise interpretation in a final Remarks section, outside the Counterexample proof.

correction: Appended a slit-disc TikZ illustration with excluded boundary/slit, excluded origin cross, inward approaches from above and below, and branch-limit labels. Original source is retained byte-for-byte as a prefix.

diagram_math_checks.check: The radius-one circle bounds the disc; the highlighted radial segment runs along the nonnegative x-axis from the origin to its boundary. Both are explicitly declared excluded, and the origin is crossed out. The endpoint at (1,0) is already excluded by the open disc.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Statement refuted and Counterexample step 1.1 define exactly this slit disc and branch.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Approaches at a representative fixed x=0.55, from positive and negative y.
diagram_math_checks.check: The upper arrow travels downward while remaining above the slit; the lower arrow travels upward while remaining below it. Their displayed y-coordinates satisfy x²+y²<1. They stop short of the slit, so no u-value there is asserted.
diagram_math_checks.justification: At x=0.55 and |y|≤0.48, x²+y²≤0.5329<1. The slit removes only y=0 with x≥0.

diagram_math_checks.check: For 0<x<1, arg(x+iy)=arctan(y/x) above the slit tends to 0 as y↓0; below, 2π−arctan(|y|/x) tends to 2π as y↑0. The arrows and labels have those orientations.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Counterexample steps 4.1 and 4.2 give these exact formulas and their one-sided extensions; the added caption extends the elementary formulas to every fixed 0<x<1.

diagram_math_checks.check: Smoothness implies continuity at (x,0), so both one-sided limits equal φ_j(x,0). The figure asserts no approximation convergence, only the local geometry and branch limits.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The original Statement and steps 4.1–5.1 use the same globally smooth boundary value in both endpoint estimates. Those estimates and the contradiction are unchanged; the proof remains independent of the figure.
